newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela jail isle suffers historic car crime.
newsitem.headline: Mandela jail isle suffers historic car crime.

text.p: South African police thought on Tuesday they had their first ever case of car theft on Robben Island, the penal colony where Nelson Mandela spent 18 years, but quickly realised they would never make the charge stick.
"You could never get a car off there unless you put it on skis," a police spokesman said. "So we're investigating a case of using a motor vehicle without the owner's consent."
He said suspects were limited, but no arrests had been made.
About 100 people live on the island which measures five km by 11 km (three miles by seven), most of them civil servants.
The island, eight km (five miles) off Cape Town, can only be reached by government-run ferry.
On January 1, its jail, whose last prisoners left in December, was declared a museum of the anti-apartheid struggle.
The stolen car was recovered almost immediately its loss was noticed on Sunday morning.
